subject: Re: Feature parity + streaming/function-calling tests \u0014 next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: feature parity + streaming/function-calling tests  recap & next steps

Alex  great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery and competitive evaluation discussion: 

1) Goals from Acme
- Validate parity for function/tool calling (webhook + structured JSON outputs) vs your current hyperscaler setup
- Measure streaming latency and early-token jitter under your typical load (12 20 RPS peak)
- Compare output fidelity for structured responses (invoices, customer summaries) and error/hallucination rates

2) Redwood differentiators to validate
- Streaming that supports incremental structured output (partial JSON + schema enforcement)
- Transparent per-token latency + cost breakdowns in Console for the test window
- Built-in function/tool calling primitives and automatic retry/fallback to a safe model variant

3) Proposed tests (we suggested during the call)
- Function-calling: run your webhook-backed flow with our function schema (well provide example handlers)  200 calls over 30 minutes, log success/failure, and verify strict JSON schema conformance
- Streaming: stream responses for 3 prompt classes (short single-turn, medium multi-instruction, long retrieval-augmented responses) and capture first-byte latency and token-rate variance
- Fidelity: run your 100-case prompt suite (attached acme-prompt-suite.csv) and evaluate structured-field accuracy and hallucination flags

Logistics / asks
- Can you confirm a 2-hour window next week (Mon/Tue preferred) for the live run?
- Please share an IP allowlist and the webhook endpoint for function-calling tests (or we can run via a secure tunnel)
- We attached a concise test plan (redwood-feature-parity-test-plan.pdf) and the prompt suite for your review

Well have a small team on the call: me (sales + PM), Vivek (solutions engineering). If you want Redwood engineering on a parallel debug channel, say the word and well loop them in.

Thanks  looking forward to getting these tests scheduled.
—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Follow-up: feature parity + streaming/function-calling tests  recap & next steps

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes/questions from our side: 

- We definitely want to validate function-calling behavior; our current infra uses a mix of synchronous webhooks and a serverless fallback. Key metrics for us are strict schema conformance and failure modes (timeouts, partial responses).
- Streaming: our main concern is early-token latency and how partial outputs are handled when downstream parsers expect valid JSON. Does Redwood provide partial-JSON safeguards or enforced schema until final token?
- Cost: curious to see per-token cost delta vs our current hyperscaler (we can share recent usage numbers offline)

We can do the live run next Tuesday 2026-12-01 between 10:00 12:00 PT. That works for our infra team. Will need IP allowlist details and a short NDA addendum before we provide production webhook endpoints.

Ive looped in Dana (infra lead) to handle logistics on our side. Thanks  looking forward to the tests.


Alex Chen
Senior Product Manager, AI Platform
Acme Corp
alex.chen@acme.com

Thanks Alex  Tuesday 2026-12-01 10:00 12:00 PT is locked from our side. A few practical items and technical details so your infra team can prep: 

1) IPs / connectivity\- We can run tests via a short-lived tunnel (ngrok-style) if you prefer not to whitelist. If you want direct calls, please provide the CIDR/IP allowlist and well add it to our staging cluster.

2) Streaming behavior and partial JSON\- Redwood supports "streaming with structured deltas": the runtime emits partial tokens but can optionally buffer up to the next JSON token boundary and include a chunked "schema-safe" flag. For the test we suggest enabling strict schema mode so the endpoint only returns chunk boundaries that leave the JSON parseable by incremental parsers. Well send the exact flag to set in the SDK request.

3) Function-calling test details\- Well provide a small Node + Python handler that validates incoming payloads. Test flow:
- Redwood receives prompt -> calls your webhook with {name, args} JSON -> expects 200 + validated JSON response within 3s
- Well run 200 calls over 30 minutes with 95th pct response-time SLAs

4) Telemetry and logs\- During the run youll get per-token latency, model variant, quantization profile, and an attachment-level CSV with the prompt and structured-field deltas. Well also publish a shared Console link for live metrics.

Attachments & links
- Test plan (redwood-feature-parity-test-plan.pdf)  attached
- Prompt suite (acme-prompt-suite.csv)  attached
- Live metrics link (will be active for the window): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-tests

If Dana can confirm IP strategy and who will run the webhook endpoint, well drop the SDK flags and the handler code.


Marissa

Marissa  forwarding internal notes for the run. Please add to the ticket. Key engineering checklist: 
- Prepare strict-schema streaming flag in SDK and run local parser against partial chunks
- Ensure function-calling retries use idempotency keys (we'll provide header X-Redwood-Idempotency)
- Enable fallback to a smaller quantized variant if we see >20% 95th pct latency spikes to avoid timeouts
- Pre-warm KV cache for retrieval-augmented prompts (we expect some long-context tests)

Also attaching the small harness well use for latency sampling in the Console (internal artifact). Ill be on the call 10:00 12:00 PT.
